audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 702441) held an idle transaction for 4.1 seconds, blocking checkout and degrading success to 7% against a 95% SLO. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting, but the trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$254,391 in lost revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance, while terminating the idempotent job cost only a 4-minute replay. The Continuity Guardian required change-calendar evidence (invariant I2), which confirmed no active window covered the batch job. After the evidence was supplied, both guardians agreed to terminate the blocker. Execution terminated the session, and verification confirmed checkout recovered to 100% success with no lock waits and no protected settlements affected.
audit.root_cause: A long-running replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile) held an idle-in-transaction lock that blocked checkout sessions, collapsing success to 7%.
lessons: For inventory_reconcile (batch_replayable_inventory), pre-load the workload registry and change-calendar status into the runbook so the Database Guardian can propose terminate immediately without a revision round.
Add a lock-timeout or statement-timeout for batch_replayable_inventory workers to prevent idle-in-transaction blocks from persisting beyond a few seconds.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted Round 1 by proposing wait despite clear evidence the blocker would not finish soon (expected 896s remaining) and the business tolerance was only 60s; the Continuity Guardian correctly enforced invariant I2, causing a necessary but avoidable revision round.
follow_ups: Update the inventory_reconcile runbook with pre-checked workload registry and change-calendar links.
Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_worker role to 30s.
Add a Prometheus alert on pg_locks waiting >10s for application_name='batch_replayable_inventory'.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 702441) is a batch_replayable_inventory worker idle in transaction for only 4.1s with last statement 'SELECT 1'. Checkout is degraded (55% success per TEL-1, 77% per BIZ-1) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation (BIZ-1).
